prompt: Seldom ___ such a well-organised conference as the one in Lisbon last spring.

explanation.rule: Tras adverbios negativos o restrictivos (Seldom, Rarely) al inicio de la frase se invierte: auxiliar + sujeto + verbo.

wrong.I have attended: Sin inversión. En español decimos "Pocas veces he asistido…", pero en inglés, tras "Seldom" inicial, el auxiliar va delante del sujeto.
wrong.have attended I: El sujeto no va al final: solo se invierte el auxiliar (have I attended), no el verbo principal.
wrong.I did attend: Sigue sin inversión; además "did" enfático no encaja con el presente perfecto que pide la experiencia.

examples: Seldom have I seen him so angry.
Rarely does she take a day off.

prompt: Little ___ that the police had been watching him for months.

explanation.rule: "Little did + sujeto + verbo" es una inversión literaria que significa "no tenía ni idea de que…".

wrong.he knew: Falta la inversión: con "Little" al principio con sentido negativo se necesita did + sujeto.
wrong.knew he: En inglés moderno no se invierte el verbo léxico; se usa el auxiliar did: did he know.
wrong.he did know: "he did know" es afirmación enfática (sí lo sabía), justo lo contrario del sentido de "Little".

examples: Little did we realise how difficult it would be.
Little did she know that her life was about to change.

prompt: Under no circumstances ___ to leave the building while the inspection is taking place.

explanation.rule: Las expresiones negativas como "Under no circumstances" o "On no account" al inicio exigen inversión: are staff allowed.

wrong.staff are allowed: Orden normal sin inversión; tras "Under no circumstances" inicial el auxiliar va antes del sujeto.
wrong.allowed are staff: Se invierte solo el auxiliar con el sujeto; el participio "allowed" no se adelanta.
wrong.staff aren't allowed: Doble negación: "Under no circumstances" ya es negativo, así que el verbo va en afirmativo (y con inversión).

examples: Under no circumstances should you open this door.
On no account must the alarm be switched off.

prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Only when I got home I realised I had lost my keys.
Only when did I get home I realised I had lost my keys.
Only when I got home I did realise I had lost my keys.
Only when I got home did I realise I had lost my keys.

explanation.rule: Con "Only when/after/once…" la inversión va en la oración principal, no en la subordinada: Only when I got home did I realise…

wrong.Only when I got home I realised I had lo: Falta la inversión en la oración principal: did I realise.
wrong.Only when did I get home I realised I ha: La inversión está en el sitio equivocado: se invierte la oración principal, no la que va con "when".
wrong.Only when I got home I did realise I had: "I did realise" mantiene el orden sujeto + auxiliar; debe ser auxiliar + sujeto: did I realise.

examples: Only after the meeting had ended did they announce the results.
Only once you have signed can we process the order.

prompt: So ___ that the final had to be postponed until the following day.

explanation.rule: "So + adjetivo + be + sujeto + that…" es una inversión enfática formal: So heavy was the rain that…

wrong.the rain was heavy: Tras "So" inicial el adjetivo debe ir pegado a "So" y luego el verbo antes del sujeto.
wrong.heavy the rain was: Orden de español ("tan fuerte la lluvia era"); en inglés el verbo va antes del sujeto: heavy was the rain.
wrong.was the rain heavy: El adjetivo debe ir inmediatamente después de "So": So heavy was the rain.

examples: So complex was the problem that nobody could solve it.
So quickly did he speak that I missed half of it.

prompt: ___ any further assistance, please do not hesitate to contact our customer service team.

explanation.rule: "Should + sujeto + verbo" sustituye a "If you need" en registro formal (condicional con inversión).

wrong.Would you need: "Would" no se usa para la inversión condicional; con este sentido solo vale "Should".
wrong.Had you needed: "Had you needed" es tercer condicional (pasado irreal) y no encaja con una petición presente como "please do not hesitate".
wrong.If you would need: No se usa "would" tras "if" en este tipo de condicional; sería "If you need" o "Should you need".

examples: Should you have any questions, please call us.
Should the flight be delayed, we will inform you by text.

prompt: ___ the support of my family, I would never have finished my degree.

explanation.rule: "Had it not been for…" = "If it hadn't been for…" (sin…). En la inversión condicional la negación no se contrae.

wrong.Hadn't it been for: En la inversión condicional no se usa la forma contraída: Had it not been for.
wrong.Had not it been for: "not" va después del sujeto: Had it not, no Had not it.
wrong.Were it not been for: Mezcla dos estructuras: "Were it not for" (presente) y "Had it not been for" (pasado); "Were… been" es incorrecto.

examples: Had it not been for the map, we would have got lost.
Had it not been for her advice, I would have made a terrible mistake.

prompt: ___ the offer, I would have to move to Dublin, which I'm not sure I want to do.

explanation.rule: "Were I to + infinitivo" = "If I were to…": condicional hipotético formal con inversión.

wrong.I were to accept: Sin "If" hace falta la inversión: Were I to accept.
wrong.Would I accept: "Would" convierte la frase en pregunta; no sirve para la condición.
wrong.Were I accept: Falta "to": la estructura es Were + sujeto + to + infinitivo.

examples: Were I to lose my job, I would retrain as a teacher.
Were she to call, tell her I'm busy.

prompt: The doctor insisted that he ___ smoking immediately.

explanation.rule: Tras insist/demand/recommend/suggest + that se usa el subjuntivo: el infinitivo sin "to" para todas las personas (he stop).

wrong.to stop: Tras "that" va una oración con sujeto y verbo; no lleva "to". "insisted that he to stop" es incorrecto.
wrong.stopping: El gerundio no puede ser el verbo de la oración con "that he…".
wrong.will stop: "will" no se usa para expresar lo que alguien exige; el subjuntivo inglés es la forma base (stop).

examples: She insisted that he be present at the meeting.
They demanded that the company pay compensation.

prompt: It is essential that every applicant ___ a copy of their passport before the interview.

explanation.rule: Tras "It is essential/vital/imperative that…" se usa el subjuntivo: la forma base del verbo.

wrong.submitting: El gerundio no puede funcionar como verbo principal de la oración "that every applicant…".
wrong.submitted: El pasado no encaja: es un requisito presente/futuro y la norma pide la forma base (submit).
wrong.to submit: Con "that + sujeto" no se usa "to"; sería "It is essential for every applicant to submit…".

examples: It is vital that she arrive on time.
It is imperative that the data be kept secure.

prompt: The committee recommended that the proposal ___ until next year.

explanation.rule: Subjuntivo pasivo: be + participio (that the proposal be postponed), sin cambiar "be" según el sujeto.

wrong.to be postponed: Tras "that + sujeto" no va "to": the proposal be postponed.
wrong.being postponed: El gerundio no funciona como verbo de la oración con "that".
wrong.will postpone: Es activa (la propuesta no aplaza nada, es aplazada) y además no es subjuntivo.

examples: They asked that the meeting be cancelled.
I suggest that the matter be discussed in private.

prompt: Which sentence is correct in formal English?
options: She demanded him to apologise at once.
She demanded that he apologise at once.
She demanded that he to apologise at once.
She demanded that he apologising at once.

explanation.rule: "Demand" no admite objeto + infinitivo; se usa demand that + sujeto + forma base (subjuntivo).

Calco del español "le exigió que…" con estructura de "ask him to"; "demand" no funciona así.
wrong.She demanded that he to apologise at onc: Tras "that he" no va "to": that he apologise.
wrong.She demanded that he apologising at once: El gerundio no puede ser el verbo de la oración subordinada.

examples: The union demanded that wages be increased.
He demanded that she tell him the truth.

prompt: ___ you won the lottery, what would you do first?

explanation.rule: "Supposing/Suppose (that)" = "Imagina que…" introduce una situación hipotética, como "if".

wrong.Provided: "Provided" expresa una condición necesaria (siempre que), no una hipótesis imaginaria en una pregunta.
wrong.Unless: "Unless" = "a menos que"; "a menos que ganaras la lotería, ¿qué harías?" no tiene sentido.
wrong.Otherwise: "Otherwise" (si no, de lo contrario) no introduce una condición al inicio de la frase.

examples: Supposing it rains, shall we still go?
Suppose you lost your passport, who would you call?

prompt: You can borrow my car, ___ you bring it back with a full tank.

explanation.rule: "Provided (that) / Providing" = "siempre que, con tal de que": condición necesaria.

wrong.unless: "unless" = "a menos que": daría el sentido contrario (puedes usarlo si NO lo devuelves lleno).
wrong.in case: "in case" = "por si acaso", no expresa una condición: no es "siempre que".
wrong.otherwise: "otherwise" significa "de lo contrario" y no puede unir así las dos oraciones.

examples: I'll come, provided that I finish work early.
Providing the weather is good, we'll eat outside.

prompt: ___ your help, we would never have met the deadline.

explanation.rule: "But for + sustantivo" = "de no ser por / sin": condicional formal sin "if".

wrong.Except for: "Except for" significa "excepto", no "de no ser por"; no crea condición.
wrong.Without of: Calco de "sin de"; "without" no lleva "of" (sería "Without your help").
wrong.If not: "If not" no puede ir seguido directamente de un sustantivo; sería "If it hadn't been for".

examples: But for the traffic, we'd have arrived on time.
But for his quick reaction, there would have been an accident.

prompt: We'd better leave now; ___, we'll miss the last train home.

explanation.rule: "Otherwise" = "si no / de lo contrario": introduce la consecuencia de no cumplir lo anterior.

wrong.unless: "unless" necesita una oración condicional detrás (unless we hurry); aquí no encaja.
wrong.provided: "provided" introduce una condición, no la consecuencia negativa.
wrong.supposing: "supposing" plantea una hipótesis; no significa "de lo contrario".

examples: Write it down; otherwise you'll forget.
I'm glad you called, otherwise I'd have waited all day.

prompt: The bank agreed to lend us the money ___ we paid it back within two years.

explanation.rule: "On condition that" = "con la condición de que": la preposición correcta es "on".

wrong.in condition that: Error de preposición: es "on condition that", no "in".
wrong.with the condition of: Calco de "con la condición de"; además no puede ir seguido de una oración (we paid).
wrong.under condition: No es una expresión fija en inglés; la correcta es "on condition that".

examples: You can go on condition that you're back by midnight.
He was released on condition that he left the country.

prompt: She ___ forgotten about the meeting; it's been in her calendar for weeks and she reminded us about it yesterday.

explanation.rule: "Could hardly have + participio" = "es casi imposible que…": deducción negativa sobre el pasado.

wrong.may well have: "may well have" indica que es bastante probable, pero el contexto (ella misma lo recordó) lo hace casi imposible.
wrong.must have: "must have" afirma que seguro lo olvidó, lo contrario de lo que indica el contexto.
wrong.should have: "should have forgotten" significaría que olvidarlo era lo correcto o lo esperado; no tiene sentido.

examples: He could hardly have known about it; nobody told him.
They could hardly have chosen a worse day.

prompt: Don't worry if he hasn't replied. He ___ been in meetings all afternoon; he usually is on Tuesdays.

explanation.rule: "May/might well have + participio" = "es muy posible que…": probabilidad alta sobre el pasado.

wrong.can hardly have: Indica que es casi imposible, pero el contexto (suele estar en reuniones los martes) lo hace probable.
wrong.must not have: Expresa certeza de que no estuvo en reuniones, lo contrario de lo que sugiere el contexto.
wrong.would rather have: "would rather have" expresa preferencia, no probabilidad, y no encaja con "been in meetings".

examples: She may well have missed the bus.
The letter might well have been lost in the post.

prompt: If you had called me at nine o'clock last night, I ___ dinner, so I wouldn't have answered.

explanation.rule: "Would have been + -ing": acción en progreso en un pasado hipotético (condicional perfecto continuo).

wrong.would be had: Forma inexistente: mezcla condicional y pasiva sin sentido.
wrong.will have been having: Es futuro perfecto continuo; aquí hablamos de una situación hipotética pasada.
wrong.had been having: El pasado perfecto va en la condición (if), no en el resultado; en el resultado se usa would.

examples: If you'd come at noon, we would have been sleeping.
I would have been working anyway, so I couldn't have helped.

prompt: A friend turns up at your door without warning and you say: "You might have told me you were coming!" What does this express?
options: Una certeza: seguro que me lo dijiste.
Una posibilidad: quizá me lo dijiste.
Una queja: deberías habérmelo dicho y no lo hiciste.
Una obligación futura: tendrás que decírmelo.

explanation.rule: "You might/could have + participio" con tono de reproche = "podrías haber…": crítica por no haber hecho algo.

La certeza se expresa con "must have"; además el amigo NO avisó.
En otro contexto sería posibilidad, pero aquí la exclamación y la visita sin aviso muestran reproche.
wrong.Una obligación futura: tendrás que decír: "might have + participio" se refiere al pasado, no a una obligación futura.

examples: You might have asked before borrowing my car!
He could have at least said thank you.

prompt: I really resent ___ what to do by people who have far less experience than I do.

explanation.rule: Pasiva con gerundio: being + participio. "Resent" va siempre seguido de gerundio.

wrong.to be told: "resent" no admite infinitivo; solo gerundio (resent being told).
wrong.be told: Tras "resent" no puede ir la forma base; hace falta el gerundio "being".
wrong.having told: Es activa: significaría que yo les digo a ellos, pero aquí me lo dicen a mí (pasiva).

examples: She hates being interrupted.
He can't stand being kept waiting.

prompt: She claims ___ about the job cuts weeks before they were officially announced.

explanation.rule: Infinitivo perfecto pasivo: to have been + participio, para algo que le ocurrió a ella antes del momento de hablar.

wrong.to be telling: Es activo y progresivo; no expresa que alguien se lo dijo a ella en el pasado.
wrong.to have told: Es activo: "tell" necesita a quién se dice. Aquí ella recibió la información, así que es pasiva.
wrong.having been told: "claim" va seguido de infinitivo, no de gerundio.

examples: He is said to have been offered a fortune.
The documents appear to have been destroyed.

prompt: Active: 'The company gave each employee a bonus.' Which passive sentence is correct?
options: Each employee was given with a bonus.
It was given each employee a bonus.
Each employee was given a bonus.
Each employee were given a bonus.

explanation.rule: Con verbos de dos objetos (give, offer, send, show) la persona suele pasar a sujeto: Each employee was given a bonus.

"give" no lleva "with"; se confunde con "provide/present someone with".
Calco de una construcción impersonal; en inglés no se usa "It" como sujeto vacío aquí.
"each employee" es singular: va con "was", no con "were".

examples: I was offered a place at the university.
We were shown the new office by the manager.

prompt: The proposal is currently ___ by the board, so we won't know the outcome until next week.

explanation.rule: Pasiva continua: is/are + being + participio, para una acción que se está haciendo ahora sobre el sujeto.

wrong.considering: Es activa: significaría que la propuesta está considerando algo.
wrong.been considered: "is been" no existe; tras "is" la pasiva continua necesita "being".
wrong.to consider: "is to consider" expresaría un plan u obligación activa y no encaja con "by the board".

examples: The road is being repaired.
Your application is being processed.

prompt: All I did ___ ask him a simple question, and he completely lost his temper.

explanation.rule: "All + sujeto + did + was (+ infinitivo)" enfatiza que solo se hizo eso: All I did was ask…

wrong.did: Repite el auxiliar; el verbo que une las dos partes es "be": All I did was…
wrong.were: "All I did" es singular (lo único que hice), así que va con "was".
wrong.has: "has" no une las dos partes de la oración hendida y no concuerda con el pasado.

examples: All she wanted was a bit of peace and quiet.
All you have to do is press this button.

prompt: The reason ___ I'm calling is to confirm your appointment for Thursday.

explanation.rule: "The reason why/that + oración + is…" sirve para enfatizar la causa.

wrong.because: "The reason because" es incorrecto; "reason" ya incluye la idea de causa: The reason why.
wrong.for what: Calco de "la razón por lo que"; en inglés sería "why", "that" o "for which".
wrong.of: "The reason of" no introduce una oración; además en inglés se dice "the reason for + sustantivo".

examples: The reason why she left is still a mystery.
That's the reason why I never trust online reviews.

prompt: It's the price ___ worries me, not the quality.

explanation.rule: Oración hendida "It is + elemento enfatizado + that…": It's the price that worries me.

wrong.what: Calco de "es el precio lo que me preocupa"; en inglés con "It's…" se usa "that" (o "which"), no "what".
wrong.who: "who" es para personas; "the price" es una cosa.
wrong.it: Repite el sujeto y deja la frase sin relativo: "It's the price it worries me" es incorrecto.

examples: It was my sister that found the keys.
It's his attitude that annoys me most.

prompt: ___ about the delay, the passengers were furious when the flight was suddenly cancelled.

explanation.rule: Participio perfecto pasivo negativo: Not having been + participio = "como no les habían dicho…".

wrong.Having not told: Es activo: significaría que los pasajeros no habían dicho nada a otros.
wrong.Not telling: Activo y simultáneo: los pasajeros no contaban algo; no es el sentido.
wrong.Not been told: Falta "having": la forma correcta es Not having been told.

examples: Not having been invited, I stayed at home.
Having been warned, we took an umbrella.

prompt: ___ what to say, she simply smiled and left the room.

explanation.rule: En las oraciones de participio la negación es "not" delante del -ing: Not knowing = "como no sabía…".

wrong.Knowing not: "not" va delante del participio, no detrás.
wrong.Don't knowing: No se usa el auxiliar "don't" con el gerundio.
wrong.No knowing: "No" va con sustantivos; para negar un participio se usa "not".

examples: Not wanting to wake anyone, he took off his shoes.
Not being an expert, I can't comment.

prompt: ___ twice about his lateness, he was finally dismissed in March.

explanation.rule: Having been + participio expresa una acción pasiva anterior a la principal: "tras haber sido advertido…".

wrong.Having warned: Es activo: significaría que él advirtió a otros, pero fue él quien recibió la advertencia.
wrong.Warning: Activo y simultáneo: él estaría advirtiendo a alguien.
wrong.To be warned: El infinitivo expresa finalidad o futuro, no una acción anterior que causa el despido.

examples: Having been told the news, she called her mother.
Having been rejected twice, he decided to give up.

prompt: Check whether the files have been backed up and, if ___, do it before you leave.

explanation.rule: "If not" sustituye a una oración negativa completa (if they haven't been backed up). También: I hope not, I'm afraid not.

wrong.no: Calco de "si no"; en inglés la sustitución de una oración negativa es "if not".
wrong.don't: Falta sujeto y verbo; además el tiempo no concuerda con "have been backed up".

examples: Is it ready? If not, I'll wait.
Will it rain? I hope not.

prompt: The manager asked us to reduce costs by ten percent, and we have done ___.

explanation.rule: "Do so" sustituye a un verbo y su complemento ya mencionado, en registro formal.

wrong.it so: "do it so" es incorrecto; se usa "do so" o "do it", no ambos.
wrong.that so: "do that so" mezcla dos sustitutos; basta con "so" (o "that").
wrong.such: "done such" no es correcto; "such" necesita un sustantivo (such a thing).

examples: Please sign the form if you have not already done so.
He promised to apologise, but he never did so.

prompt: I didn't enjoy the film at all, and ___ my sister.

explanation.rule: Para añadir acuerdo con una frase negativa se usa neither/nor + auxiliar + sujeto.

wrong.so did: "so did" sirve para frases afirmativas; aquí la primera es negativa.
wrong.either did: "either" va al final de una frase negativa (my sister didn't either), no al principio con inversión.
wrong.neither didn't: Doble negación: "neither" ya es negativo, así que el auxiliar va en afirmativo.

examples: She can't swim, and neither can I.
He doesn't eat meat, nor does his wife.

prompt: The process ___ the company selects new staff is extremely rigorous.

explanation.rule: "Whereby" (= by which, mediante el cual) es un relativo formal para procesos, sistemas o acuerdos.

wrong.which: Falta la preposición: la empresa selecciona "by" ese proceso; sería "by which" o "whereby".
wrong.where by: Se escribe en una sola palabra: whereby.
wrong.whom: "whom" se refiere a personas, y "the process" es una cosa.

examples: They signed an agreement whereby profits would be shared equally.
It's a system whereby users can vote online.

prompt: She has three brothers, none of ___ live nearby.

explanation.rule: Cuantificador + of + whom/which en relativas explicativas: none of whom (personas), some of which (cosas).

wrong.them: Con "them" serían dos oraciones unidas solo por una coma, lo cual es incorrecto; se necesita el relativo "whom".
wrong.who: Después de preposición (of) se usa "whom", no "who".

examples: I bought five books, two of which were in French.
The guests, most of whom were students, left early.

prompt: The man ___ the anonymous letter was written has never been identified.

explanation.rule: En registro formal la preposición va delante del relativo: by whom (personas), in/by which (cosas).

wrong.whom: Falta la preposición "by": la carta fue escrita por ese hombre.
wrong.which by: "which" no se usa para personas y el orden es preposición + relativo.

examples: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
She is the author by whom the novel was translated.

prompt: The flat ___ we lived for ten years has just been sold.

explanation.rule: Preposición + which en relativas formales: the flat in which we lived (= where we lived).

wrong.which: Falta la preposición: vivíamos "en" el piso (in which / which we lived in).
wrong.in that: "that" no puede ir detrás de una preposición.
wrong.where in: Orden incorrecto; se dice "in which" o simplemente "where".

examples: The hotel at which we stayed was excellent.
This is the box in which I keep my letters.

prompt: There was ___ interest in the proposal, so it was quietly dropped.

explanation.rule: "Hardly any" = "casi nada/ninguno". "Hardly" ya es negativo, así que se combina con "any".

wrong.hardly no: Doble negación: en español decimos "casi no hubo ningún…", pero en inglés "hardly" va con "any".
wrong.barely none: Doble negación; además "none" es pronombre y no puede ir delante de un sustantivo.

examples: We have hardly any milk left.
Hardly anyone came to the talk.

prompt: ___ of the respondents said they would prefer to work from home at least two days a week.

explanation.rule: "The vast majority of" = "la gran mayoría de": colocación fija con "vast".

wrong.The big majority: Traducción literal de "la gran mayoría"; en inglés la colocación natural es "vast".
wrong.The vast most: "most" no se combina con "vast" ni con "the" en este sentido.
wrong.Vast majority: Falta el artículo: the vast majority.

examples: The vast majority of students passed.
A vast majority of voters supported the plan.

prompt: Although the theory was widely publicised, ___ scientists took it seriously, and it was soon forgotten.

explanation.rule: "Few" (sin artículo) = "pocos, casi ninguno" con sentido negativo; "a few" = "unos cuantos" con sentido positivo.

wrong.a little: "a little" va con incontables; "scientists" es contable plural.
wrong.a few: "a few" tiene sentido positivo (algunos sí); no explica que la teoría se olvidara pronto.
wrong.little: "little" se usa con incontables, no con "scientists".

examples: Few people know the real story.
Very few applicants met all the requirements.

prompt: We ___ leave when the phone rang, so we missed the start of the concert.

explanation.rule: "Was/were about to + infinitivo" = "estaba a punto de" en el pasado.

wrong.were on the verge to: "on the verge" va con "of + -ing" (on the verge of leaving), no con "to".
wrong.are about to: Presente; la acción ocurrió en el pasado (the phone rang).

examples: I was about to call you.
The film was about to start when the power went off.

prompt: The ceremony ___ held in June, but the storm forced the organisers to cancel it.

explanation.rule: "Was to have been + participio" expresa un plan del pasado que no llegó a cumplirse.

wrong.was going to have: Necesita pasiva: "was going to be held"; con "have held" la ceremonia celebraría algo.
wrong.would be to: "would be to held" es incorrecto: tras "to" iría la forma base y además no expresa un plan frustrado.
wrong.is to have been: El presente no concuerda con un plan pasado que se canceló.

examples: She was to have started work on Monday, but she fell ill.
The bridge was to have been finished by 2020.

prompt: The company was on the verge ___ bankrupt when a new investor stepped in.

explanation.rule: "Be on the verge/brink of + -ing" = "estar al borde de".

wrong.of go: Tras una preposición (of) el verbo va en -ing.

examples: She was on the verge of tears.
They were on the verge of signing the contract.

prompt: ___ the bad weather, the festival went ahead as planned.

explanation.rule: "Notwithstanding" (formal) = "a pesar de"; va seguido de un sustantivo.

wrong.Albeit: "albeit" significa "aunque" y se coloca delante de un adjetivo o adverbio, no al inicio con un sustantivo.
wrong.Whereas: "whereas" (mientras que) contrasta dos oraciones completas; aquí solo hay un sustantivo.
wrong.Insofar as: "insofar as" significa "en la medida en que" y necesita una oración detrás.

examples: Notwithstanding the cost, they bought the house.
The plan was approved, notwithstanding some objections.

prompt: The results were encouraging, ___ based on a very small sample.

explanation.rule: "Albeit" = "aunque, si bien": introduce una concesión breve sin verbo conjugado.

wrong.although of: "although" no lleva "of"; "although based on…" sería posible, pero "although of" no.
wrong.whereas: "whereas" contrasta dos hechos distintos y necesita una oración con verbo.
wrong.despite: "despite" va con sustantivo o -ing; "despite based" es incorrecto.

examples: It was a success, albeit a limited one.
He agreed, albeit reluctantly.

prompt: What does 'insofar as' mean in: 'The plan is fair insofar as everyone pays the same amount.'?

explanation.rule: "Insofar as" = "en la medida en que, en tanto que": limita hasta qué punto algo es cierto.

wrong.siempre que: Eso sería "provided that" o "as long as" (condición).

examples: I agree with you insofar as the costs are concerned.
The report is useful insofar as it identifies the problems.

prompt: We regret ___ you that your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion.

explanation.rule: "Regret to + infinitivo" = "lamentar comunicar" (fórmula formal); "regret + -ing" = arrepentirse de algo ya hecho.

wrong.informing: "regret informing" significaría arrepentirse de haberle informado, no lamentar comunicarle algo ahora.
wrong.to have informed: Hablaría de una información pasada; la carta comunica la noticia en este momento.
wrong.inform: "regret" no va seguido de la forma base sin "to".

examples: I regret to say that the shop is closing.
I regret not studying harder at school.

prompt: After discussing the budget, the director went on ___ the plans for the new office.

explanation.rule: "Go on to + infinitivo" = pasar a hacer otra cosa; "go on + -ing" = seguir haciendo lo mismo.

wrong.explaining: "went on explaining" = siguió explicando lo mismo; aquí cambia de tema (del presupuesto a los planes).
wrong.explain: "go on" no va seguido de la forma base.
wrong.to explaining: "to" aquí es parte del infinitivo, así que va con la forma base: to explain.

examples: She went on to become a famous writer.
He went on talking even though nobody was listening.

prompt: Taking the new job would mean ___ to another city, so I need some time to think about it.

explanation.rule: "Mean + -ing" = implicar, suponer; "mean to + infinitivo" = tener la intención de.

wrong.to move: "mean to move" significaría "tener la intención de mudarme"; el sujeto es "taking the job", que implica, no pretende.
wrong.move: "mean" no va seguido de la forma base.

examples: Being a nurse means working at weekends.
I didn't mean to upset you.
